verdict_a_reason: The real browser watch journal records admission, a healthy watch, stop confirmation, and a final decision under one run ID; its retained SHA-256 matches the implementation report. A mid-run writer fault makes the first isolated browser run resourceInvalid with exit 3, retains its lease, and refuses the next launch as stale. The finalization correction writes to a pending path, closes the descriptor, and only then atomically publishes the completed path. A failed close exits 3 and leaves no completed verdict, even when the pending file contains a valid-looking final event.
verdict_b_reason: The publication boundary resolves the prior close-failure mismatch without changing admission caps or allowlisted commands. Journal writes are synchronous, bounded to guard fields, private, and exclusive by run ID. The code retains the permit after a writer fault, and the new tests exercise the close seam at both helper and wrapper levels. No actionable requirement flaw was found within the documented cooperative process contract.

prior_finding_final_close_failure.evidence: scripts/stabilization-resource-journal.mjs closes the pending file before linkSync publishes the completed file. The injected wrapper close failure exits 3, prints RESOURCE_JOURNAL_FINALIZE_FAILED, and leaves only the pending file. docs/stabilization/PLAN.md says pending files cannot establish a resource verdict.

limits: This review inspected and hashed retained live browser journals; it did not repeat a 60-second preflight, open UI, run localhost, or induce a physical disk failure. The injected close failure uses an isolated copied helper and a denied command, so the browser lease conclusion also relies on the retained isolated mid-run writer-fault evidence and direct review of the guard's finally branch.
